raw_response:
I’m an old hand at this, so I won’t change too much unless there’s a clear reason. On my 2 mu, wheat and maize are still the safest way. Wheat keeps the land busy through winter and gives steady grain, then maize follows right after harvest, so even if one season is just average, the whole year is still workable. I have well water, so I’m not completely at the mercy of the sky, but pumping costs money, so I won’t irrigate more than needed. With only 2 mu and 3 people in the house, family labor is enough, and I’d rather spend carefully than chase some very high target yield.

For wheat, I’ll sow in the normal October window with a common improved local variety, not anything fancy. I usually put most fertilizer at the start, then watch the crop at jointing and give topdressing if the leaves are pale and the stand looks weak. Wheat matters because if the base is poor, the whole year feels tight. After wheat harvest in June, I’ll move quickly into summer maize. The turnaround is short in Quzhou, so I won’t do heavy tillage, just quick land prep and planting. For maize I still use hybrid seed because the stand is better and yield is more reliable. I’ll keep fertilizer moderate, not too low because that risks losing yield, but not too high either because on 2 mu every extra bag is cash out of pocket.
